run_joint.A1_r3_own_adam.final.definition: final metric record of a read-out-only run on R3's frozen states (R3 read-in + frozen LSTM, joint read-out from W = 0, batch 8,000 of 54,000 pool episodes, held-out episodes 54,000-59,999). acc_T30: held-out goal accuracy at t = 30 (argmax of the goal marginal); n_excluded: cells whose fixed (training-episode-mean) logit table at t = 30, F_30 = W M_30 + 30 c, is > 10 nats below the best cell of its row AND of its column (of 100); n_frozen_rows: read-out rows whose median Adam sqrt(v_hat) is below eps = 1e-8; E_fix_t: energy (sum of squares) of the double-centred part of the fixed logit table at step t (the fixed coupling); label: convergence label from the change over the last 20% of updates (run_joint rule: 'still rising (lower bound)' if the accuracy rise >= 0.01; 'accuracy flat, loss still falling' if the loss fell by >= 2%; else 'converged')

convergence.label: converged
convergence.definition:
change of held-out accuracy (T=30) and of the held-out loss of the run's own type over the last 20% of updates.
        rise_last20 = least-squares slope over the metric records with update >= 0.8 * updates, times 0.2 * updates.
        Label: 'still rising (lower bound)' if the accuracy rise >= 0.01; else 'accuracy flat, loss still falling' if
        the loss fell by >= 2% (relative); else 'declining' if the accuracy fell by >= 0.01; else 'converged'.

final.check1.learning_order.definition:
Check 1 (synthesis_final, CPU, 3 threads): LEARNING ORDER of the memoryless per-step nets, from their stored snapshots.

Question (critic gap 2; John's "general prior"): does a one-layer per-step learner pick up the per-bit (naive) part of
the target first and never the within-step part W (an inductive-bias / learning-order "prior"), and does training make
its read-in MORE affine in the bits, as R1's read-in became (non-affine share 8.8% at init -> 3.3%)?

Nets (run_marginal, seed 0, width 1000, batch 2000, Adam 1e-3, fresh environments; read only):
  e2e_d1_s0: m1 (marginal, own loss), m1g (marginal, goalCE), j1 (joint, joint KL), j2 (joint, own loss)
             snapshots u = 0, 10, 100, 1000, 2500, 5000, 12500, 25000 (final_nets.pt)
  e2e_d2_s0: m2 (marginal, depth 2, own loss) snapshots u = 0 (rebuilt: torch.manual_seed(0) then MemNet, as the
             trainer), 1000, 5000, 12500, 24352
Two measurements per snapshot:
 (A) FEATURE CAPTURE, exactly theory_marg c3's protocol (copied): hidden features h(o, z) (the last ReLU layer) of 120,000
     training samples (z of pool environments 0-53,999, uniform cell, o drawn from it) and 30,000 held-out samples
     (environments 54,000-59,999); one SHARED least-squares read-out (+ constant, ridge 1e-8 tr(G)/d) per target;
     held-out R^2 for N (naive per-step part), W (within-step part = step-wise - naive), f (step-wise per-step marginal
     log-likelihood), joint (per-step joint evidence, 100 cells); within-environment NON-AFFINE share of the features
     (200 held-out environments x 32 bit patterns, unweighted: share of the features' within-environment variance not
     explained by an affine function of the 5 bits). Same seeds as c3, so R1's read-in values (0.977 / 0.284 / 0.794 /
     0.973, non-affine 0.0335) and the PyTorch-init values (0.434 / 0.032 / 0.322 / 0.399, 0.081) are comparable.
 (B) OUTPUT COEFFICIENTS (marginal nets): the net's per-step goal-latent logits (centred over the 10 values) on the
     pool's held-out episodes 54,000-56,999 (each episode's own goal), regressed without intercept on naive's centred
     per-step log-likelihood N and on the step-wise rule's centred per-step log-likelihood f = N + W:
     y ~ a N + b f  ->  coefficient on N = a + b, on W = b (run_marginal analyze_marg's pair regression); single-rule
     R^2 for N and f; T = 30 accuracy of the summed outputs on these episodes.
Writes ../out/lo_check.json (incrementally). Nothing is written outside synthesis_final.
